quote: The way the program is currently set up is there is no out of pocket cost during the upfront fees. All we're doing is what's called a bill swap
stewart_read: Rep explains the bill-swap financial mechanism in detail instead of using the escape hatch to redirect to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be trying to preempt customer confusion before continuing verify — but the level of financial detail given exceeds what's needed to keep the call moving.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch ('that's exactly what our specialist covers') instead of explaining bill-swap mechanics live.

quote: So what credit score? Like, why are you asking for the credit?
stewart_read: Customer's credit-score pushback is a mild skepticism objection; rep gives a flat procedural reason instead of a bill-anchored flip.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported — no flip was attempted anywhere in the call despite the bill amount later being captured.
coaching_implication: Tie the credit ask back to their own bill pain (already captured as $80-something/month) instead of a generic incentive-qualification line.

quote: Let me just try shooting you in from my personal number then because I don't know why it wasn't
stewart_read: Rep gives out a personal phone number to work around a text-delivery failure, matching the flagged anti-pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive necessity — no automated fallback exists yet, so the rep's workaround was the only path to unblock the bill capture in real time.
coaching_implication: Escalate to a company-sanctioned number or defer bill capture to the specialist visit rather than sharing a personal line.

quote: I remember last month, it was five zero five.
stewart_read: Customer hands over a concrete usage anchor (505 kWh) and rep files it flatly without reflecting it back as a forward-pulling hook.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this a data point only, not an emotional lever, since usage (not dollar bill) was given here.
coaching_implication: Reflect usage numbers back with a light hook, e.g. acknowledging that's a meaningful load worth designing around, to build anticipation for the specialist meeting.

quote: Do you know how much is the average, like, you guys charge for, beer, kilo?
stewart_read: Rep correctly declines to answer a pricing question and redirects to the specialist meeting.
coaching_implication: This is the correct move — hold up as the model example of scope discipline for this rep.

quote: Oh, so we have to buy them or it's for free now?
stewart_read: Second touch of the same cost-mechanism question; rep again explains program structure instead of deferring.
coaching_implication: Same escape-hatch fix as the first touch — this recurrence shows the rep defaults to explaining rather than redirecting under any cost question.

quote: Yeah. So it would not bring anything from out of pocket. Right?
stewart_read: Third touch of the cost/mechanism thread; rep reconfirms no out-of-pocket cost rather than pivoting to the specialist.
coaching_implication: Pattern across all three touches: rep should route cost questions to the specialist meeting instead of building out the financial explanation piecemeal.
